ev.text:
As of my latest knowledge, the UK ETA cost £10 per person when it launched in 2023, and it rose to **£16 per person** from 9 April 2025. I can't check live government sources, so please confirm the current fee on GOV.UK before applying, since it could have changed by November 2026.

Apply only through the official UK ETA app or the GOV.UK website, as third-party sites often add extra fees. The ETA is valid for multiple visits over two years (or until your passport expires, if sooner), and each traveller, including children, needs their own.

receipts.question: How much does a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) cost to apply for?
receipts.answer: An ETA costs £20, according to the GOV.UK ETA page (dated 22 October 2026) [1]. The Home Office's April 2026 factsheet also gives £20 and notes that the fee is kept under review [2]. The ETA is valid for up to two years, or until the passport expires if that comes sooner, and covers multiple journeys of up to six months each [2].

items.question: As of November 2026, what is the newest stable feature (minor) release of Python?

ev.text:
As of November 2026, the newest stable feature release should be **Python 3.14**, which came out in October 2025. Python 3.15 is on track for release in October 2026 under the annual schedule (PEP 790), so it may already be out by now. I can't confirm that from memory, so check python.org/downloads to be sure.

My knowledge doesn't reliably extend to the 3.15 final release. If it has shipped, 3.15 is the newest stable feature release. Otherwise 3.14 is, with 3.15 still in release-candidate stage.

notes.focus: Identify the newest stable minor release of Python as of November 2026, given the sources' dates and version information.

keyPoints.text: Python 3.15.0 is the stable major release, released 9 October 2026, described as the newest major release.
Python 3.15 is the newest minor series; 3.15.2 is its latest maintenance release (25 Oct 2026).
Python 3.14 is the previous stable series, with latest 3.14.10 (25 Oct 2026), and 3.15 is listed as the current feature release series.
Python 3.15.0b2 was superseded by 3.15.2 and the 3.15 series is no longer in development.

Source 1 dated 2026-10-21 lists 3.16 as having a release schedule, which predates the 3.15.2 date and may not reflect current status.
